display.title: Episode 228: King David's Grave (Before Shavuos)
display.summary_short: The week before Shavuos: the mitzvah of Shavuos is the whole Torah, a yeshiva boy says the Shema, and a rabbi retrieves a king's sword from the sealed cave of Dovid HaMelech.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Shavuos 5746, which fell on Friday and Shabbos. Uncle Yossi asks which mitzvah belongs to Shavuos, and answers that Shavuos stands for all 613 mitzvos: it celebrates Matan Torah, so its mitzvah is the Torah itself. We renew 'Naaseh v'nishma' with resolutions to learn more, stay up on Shavuos night with Tikkun Leil Shavuos, and receive the Torah with joy. A yeshiva boy says the Shema in Studio 604, followed by a sponsor message. The story: a visiting king wants to see the burial cave of Dovid HaMelech in Yerushalayim, which is sealed because no one who went in came out alive. When his precious royal sword slips through the bars, two servants sent down do not return. The king turns to the local rabbi, who gathers the community to say Tehillim, goes down, and comes up with the sword, telling of a bright light below. The king grants the Jews freedom to keep the Torah. The show ends with the names of children in the running in the Sefer Torah contest and an invitation to buy a letter in the children's Sefer Torah.
display.lesson: On Shavuos we receive the Torah anew: resolve to learn more Torah and do more mitzvos, with joy.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: Shavuos is 'next week, Friday and Shabbos' (6-7 Sivan 5746 = 13-14 June 1986).

advisories.note: People who enter the sealed cave, including two servants sent by the king, do not come out alive.
A rabbi is lowered into the dangerous cave while the community prays.
